content: 1. Elagolix, a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, can reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. If co-administered, consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates as needed. 2. Etravirine can decrease the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A inducers should be avoided as it may reduce the therapeutic efficacy of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Alternative drugs are recommended. 3. Etravirine reduces the plasma levels or effects of eletriptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 4. Etravirine significantly decreases the levels or effects of eliglustat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Etravirine and elivaldogene autotemcel may mutually reduce each other's effects through mechanisms not fully understood. Patients should avoid antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 6. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may lead to reduced plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and associated protease inhibitors, potentially resulting in therapeutic failure or resistance. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of encorafenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant concentrations. Alternative drugs are recommended. 8. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of entrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or substitution with an alternative drug is advised. 9. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of etravirine, and etravirine reduces the levels or effects of enzalutamide, both through CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 10. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of eplerenone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of erdafitinib via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its levels or effects through CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. 12. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ergonovine and ergotamine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 13. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of erlotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, these erythromycin formulations increase the levels or effects of etravirine. Alternative drugs are recommended. 15. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eslicarbazepine acetate via CYP3A4 metabolism, while eslicarbazepine acetate increases etravirine levels through CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism, and esomeprazole increases etravirine levels through the same pathway. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of estradiol, estradiol vaginal, conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eszopiclone, ethinylestradiol, ethosuximide, and etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of ethotoin by influencing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eucalyptus by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of exemestane by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases fedratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers has not been studied. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Felbamate increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while etravirine decreases felbamate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Felodipine increases the levels or effects of etravirine via CYP2C19 metabolism, while etravirine reduces felodipine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, therapeutic failure, or withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. After discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Alternative drugs are recommended. 29. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of fesoterodine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Etravirine also increases fexinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects, and alternative drugs are recommended. 31. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of finasteride by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 33. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of etravirine via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine reduces fludrocortisone levels through the same pathway. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Fluoxetine increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of flurazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 38. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen and fluvastatin by influencing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 39. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended.
